e-81.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^2.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{4-5x-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}+3} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(-2x-\frac{5}{x}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})}{(1+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(\frac{-2x+0+0}{1+0}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-2x) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}

e-82.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function
e-82.problem: What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ with $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^3+1}{x^3-15x}?$
e-82.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y=\lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2{x}^{3}+1}{{x}^{3}-15x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{15x}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(2+\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{15}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{2+0}{1-0} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=2.$

e-83.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
e-83.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\dfrac{x^5-10}{x^3-8x^2}.$
e-83.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y=\lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{5}-10}{{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{8{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{({x}^{2}-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}})}{(1-\frac{8}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{{x}^{2}-0}{1-0}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{4}-6}{{x}^{2}-x+2} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{({x}^{2}-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{({x}^{2}-0)}{(1-0+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: What is the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ for $x<0$ with $f(x)=\frac{|3x+6|}{x-4}?$
after.worked_solution:
For large negative values of $x,$ we have $|3x+6|=-(3x+6).$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{|3x+6|}{x-4}={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3x+6)}{x-4}.
$$

The horizontal asymptote for $x<0$ is $y={lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3x+6)}{x-4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(\frac{3x}{x}+\frac{6}{x})}{(\frac{x}{x}-\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-(3+\frac{6}{x})}{(1-\frac{4}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-(3+0)}{1-0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-3.$

content.problem: Given that the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{24{x}^{3}-1}{2c{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}}$ is $y=-\frac{1}{3},$ find the value of $c.$
content.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{24{x}^{3}-1}{2c{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{24{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2c{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{15{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(24-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(2c-\frac{15}{x})} \\  & =\frac{24-0}{2c-0} \\  & =\frac{12}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{c} & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ c & =-36.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{11{x}^{5}-9{x}^{6}}{2{x}^{5}-1}.$
after.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{11{x}^{5}-9{x}^{6}}{2{x}^{5}-1} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{11{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{9{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(11-9x)}{(2-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{11-9x}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(11-9x) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{7{x}^{5}-3{x}^{2}}{6-2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{7{x}^{5}}{x}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{x})}{(\frac{6}{x}-\frac{2x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(7{x}^{4}-3x)}{(\frac{6}{x}-2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(7{x}^{4}-3x)}{0-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(7{x}^{4}-3x) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
